chunks: Ibn Kathir al-Shami states in Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya, vol. 12, p. 15:

(He was) the Sheikh of the Imami Rafidis, their author, and the defender of their hawzah. He enjoyed prestige among the regional rulers (muluk al-atraf), on account of the inclination of many people of that era toward Shi'ism.

His scholarly gathering was attended by large numbers of scholars from all sects. Among his students were al-Sharif al-Radi and al-Murtada; and the one who eulogized him — meaning al-Murtada — did so with a qasida (elegy) after his death.

key_terms.التَّشَيُّعِ: Shi'ism — the way of following the Imams of the Ahlulbayt
key_terms.الرَّوَافِضِ: Rafidis — a pejorative designation used by some Sunni scholars for Shia Muslims
key_terms.حَوْزَتِهِمْ: their hawzah — the Shia scholarly institution and its sphere of influence
key_terms.وَجَاهَةٌ: prestige, social standing, influence among rulers and elites

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Kathir al-Shami write about Sheikh al-Mufid's scholarly status, students, and legacy in Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya?
ai.summary: Ibn Kathir al-Shami, in Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (vol. 12, p. 15), describes the subject (Sheikh al-Mufid) as the foremost Imami scholar, the principal author for the Shia, and the defender of their hawzah (scholarly sphere); he enjoyed considerable prestige among regional rulers owing to widespread Shi'i sympathies of the era. His scholarly gatherings drew scholars from every sect, and his students included al-Sharif al-Radi and al-Murtada, the latter of whom composed a funeral elegy (qasida) for him after his death.
